headline: A Certificate Transparency log-list live-fetch client ships. pki.ct.fetchLogList fetches and verifies the CT log list over HTTPS before trusting a single log.
summary: pki.ct.fetchLogList(opts) turns the shipped offline CT trust chain into a live client: it GETs the log_list.json and its detached log_list.sig over the shared fail-closed pki.transport, verifies the detached signature over the raw fetched bytes against a caller-pinned distributor key, and only on a valid signature ingests the same bytes through pki.ct.parseLogList, so it never parses, reads, caches, or surfaces any field of an unverified document (verify-before-parse). It composes pki.ct.verifyLogListSignature and pki.ct.parseLogList over the same node:https transport the EST / ACME / CMP clients use, adding no new ASN.1, crypto, or socket code. There is no baked-in vendor URL and no baked-in key: the caller points opts.url at the distributor and pins opts.signerKey out-of-band. TLS trust is explicit (an anchor set or an opt-in to the system store; server verification is always on), each response is size-capped before it reaches the trust chain, and the transport is dependency-injectable so it is fully testable offline. The parsed list's version and timestamp are surfaced (never policed) so a caller enforces its own freshness policy.

Added: pki.ct.fetchLogList(opts) fetches the Certificate Transparency log list live and returns the trusted-log set only after the detached signature verifies against the caller-pinned distributor key. It GETs opts.url (the log_list.json) and the detached opts.sigUrl (the log_list.sig, by default opts.url with a .json path suffix rewritten to .sig) over the shared pki.transport (or an injected opts.transport), verifies pki.ct.verifyLogListSignature over the raw JSON bytes against opts.signerKey, and only on a valid signature ingests the same bytes through pki.ct.parseLogList, returning { logs, byLogId, version, timestamp, raw, status, contentType, tls }. No baked-in vendor URL and no baked-in key (both are caller-pinned); explicit TLS trust (an anchor set or an opts.tls.useSystemStore opt-in, rejectUnauthorized always on); each GET is size-capped before verify/parse; every fetch / verify / parse failure is a typed CtError. RFC 6962.

pki.ct.parseLogList now also returns the document's version (a string or null) and timestamp (the parsed log_list_timestamp as a Date, or null when absent/unparseable). That is the freshness surface a caller polices, read leniently from the same document. Existing callers of the { logs, byLogId } shape are unaffected.
